definitions.explanation: An employee hired on an open-ended, full-time contract with full benefits, job security, and company protections. Distinguished from part-time, contract, or dispatch workers in the Japanese employment system.

examples.japanese: ⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{正社員|せいしゃいん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I will become a regular employee starting next year.

examples.japanese: {正社員|せいしゃいん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{非正規|ひせいき}→非正規：26236_hiseiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{待遇|たいぐう}→待遇：12517_taiguu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{差|さ}→差：02771_sa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There is a difference in treatment between regular and non-regular employees.

examples.english: More companies now have systems for promoting part-timers to regular employee status.

notes:
USAGE:
A key term in the Japanese employment system. {正社員|せいしゃいん} typically enjoy lifetime employment (⟦{終身|しゅうしん}{雇用|こよう}→終身雇用：13852_shuushinkoyou⟧), regular salary increases, bonuses, and social insurance. The distinction between {正社員|せいしゃいん} and ⟦{非正規|ひせいき}→非正規：26236_hiseiki⟧⟦{社員|しゃいん}→社員：03065_shain⟧ (non-regular workers) is a major social and economic issue in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {正社員|せいしゃいん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧: to work as a regular employee
- {正社員|せいしゃいん}⟦{登用|とうよう}→登用：17153_touyou⟧: promotion to regular employee status
- {正社員|せいしゃいん}⟦{募集|ぼしゅう}→募集：03035_boshuu⟧: recruiting for regular positions

CONTRASTING TERMS:
- ⟦{契約|けいやく}{社員|しゃいん}→契約社員：12260_keiyakushain⟧: contract employee
- ⟦{派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}→派遣社員：18875_hakenshain⟧: dispatch/temporary worker
- ⟦パート→パート：03106_paato⟧ / ⟦アルバイト→アルバイト：01528_arubaito⟧: part-time worker
